input.question: Why does poor circulation cause swelling/edema?
input.ground_truth: Blood fluid (plasma, not cells) is always leaving blood vessels and seeping into tissue because of blood pressure. If the fluid pressure in the tissues is reasonably close to the static blood pressure in the veins or the venous ends of the capillary beds, most of this fluid flows back into the veins and into circulation again. If you have poor circulation, the venous pressure rises and keeps the fluid in the tissue. u/ethicsg said that the lymphatic system does a lot of work to collect this fluid from the tissue and take it back to the blood vessels and this is true. Unfortunately, both the lymphatic system and the veins require physical muscle motion to get their fluids moving, and so if that doesn't happen then edema, or fluid buildup in tissue, can result. That was a bit wordy. In short, if your blood doesn't move, pressure builds up. If pressure builds up, blood is forced into tissues and causes edema.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why does poor circulation cause swelling/edema?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your body is like a garden with lots of tiny water pipes (these are your blood vessels). These pipes carry water (which is like your blood) to all the flowers (which are like your body parts).

If the pipes are squeezed or not working well (that’s poor circulation), the water can’t flow to the flowers as easily. So, some water gets stuck and makes the flowers swell up, just like a sponge that’s holding too much water. That swelling is called edema.

So, when circulation is poor, the water (fluid) builds up and makes things swell.
